title: Pre-training Time Series Models with Stock Data Customization

problem.claim: Stock selection aims to predict stock prices and identify the most profitable stocks.

gap.claim: Existing stock series pre-training methods largely transfer strategies from other domains without adapting to stock-specific contextual information and the non-stationary nature of stock prices, leaving latent statistical features underutilized.

contributions.claim: The paper proposes three stock-data-tailored pre-training tasks: stock code classification, stock sector classification, and moving average prediction.
The paper develops the Stock Specialized Pre-trained Transformer based on a two-layer transformer architecture.
The paper reports evaluations across five stock datasets spanning four markets and two time periods, along with simulated-data experiments to investigate underlying mechanisms.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors explicitly describe the three stock-data-tailored pre-training tasks as novel.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that extensive experiments validate the effectiveness of their pre-training methods and provide guidance on their application.
The authors report that SSPT consistently outperforms the market and existing methods on cumulative investment return ratio and Sharpe ratio across five stock datasets.
The authors report that simulated-data experiments provide insights into understanding price series and the underlying mechanisms of their methods.

narrative_sequence.summary: Stock selection seeks to predict prices and identify profitable stocks.
Pre-training strategies are underexplored and existing approaches overlook stock-specific context and non-stationarity.
The paper introduces three stock-specific pre-training tasks and the SSPT model.
Experiments on real and simulated data assess performance and investigate mechanisms.
The authors state that the code is publicly available.

source_observation.claim: The proposed pre-training tasks encode stock code, sector, and moving-average information.

interpretation.claim: Pre-training may benefit from objectives that represent domain-specific context and temporal characteristics.

application.claim: When adapting pre-training to financial time series, consider objectives tied to entity identity, domain structure, and temporal summaries.

exception.claim: The abstract does not establish which task or combination is responsible for the reported gains across other settings.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify dataset names, market identities, time periods, baselines, or numerical performance differences.
The abstract does not describe the training protocol, ablations, or implementation details beyond the two-layer transformer architecture.
The abstract does not provide details of the simulated data or the mechanisms identified by those experiments.
